clue.text: Withdrew deposit in artistic part of Paris

blocks.note: to withdraw from a place is to leave it, past tense
to deposit money is to bank it

explanation.surface: Someone takes their savings out of a bank in a bohemian quarter of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrew deposit' reads as one banking transaction, but it is two separate words: past-tense leaving, then a verb for paying money in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rive Gauche, south of the Seine, has long been the city's district of painters, writers and students.

clue.text: Clean wheels going round hard

indicators.note: something going round another thing encloses it, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: slang for a car is 'wheels'
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Instructions to scrub the tyres of a vehicle as they turn, pressing firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: To char is to work as a cleaner, as a charwoman does; a chiefly British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlady does household cleaning, so to char means to do domestic scrubbing work for pay.

clue.text: Nauseatingly suave sergeant-major in front of the soldiers

blocks.note: SM is the standard abbreviation for sergeant-major
a body of soldiers taken together

explanation.surface: An oily, ingratiating sergeant-major parades before his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes an ingratiating, oily charm that is unpleasantly smooth and insincere.

clue.text: In disorder, tho' a solver has help in another way

indicators.note: doing something in another way means arranging it differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter by letter as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled solver gets assistance with a puzzle by tackling it differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins the two parts of the fodder; all fourteen letters of 'tho' a solver' and 'help' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered everywhere in a chaotic, untidy way, a colloquial British phrase for messiness.

clue.text: Song requires absurd gear on a lady's head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its very start, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: something absurd is crazy or mad
a rig is a set of equipment or gear
taken as written
first letter of the word lady

explanation.surface: A song calls for ridiculous headgear perched on a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' looks like an anagram signal for 'gear', but it simply gives a synonym, and 'on' just places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for several unaccompanied voices, so it is a type of song.

clue.text: Soul's duty I interpreted with diligence

indicators.note: a text that is interpreted is rendered afresh in a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken letter by letter as written

explanation.surface: A believer conscientiously works out what spiritual obligations demand of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something studiously means doing it carefully and attentively, with deliberate application and effort.

clue.text: Sailor has fizzy drink to look at

blocks.note: pop is a sweet carbonated soft drink
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A seaman orders a soda and gazes at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the spinach-eating cartoon sailor man created by E. C. Segar, a famous seafaring character.

clue.text: White liquid mixture provides me with bleach

indicators.note: a mixture stirs its ingredients together, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaning product warns that its white fluid blend contains bleach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White liquid mixture' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'liquid' and 'mixture' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Béchamel is the classic French white sauce made from milk thickened with a butter-and-flour roux.

clue.text: Spirit and a fizzy tonic

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the following letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order at the bar: a spirit with a sparkling tonic water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit and a fizzy tonic' sounds like a gin and tonic order, but spirit here means liveliness, not alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit in the sense of energy and vigour matches action meaning lively activity or drive.

clue.text: This celebrity participates in dishonest arguments

indicators.note: to participate in something is to be part of it, so the word sits inside the following phrase

blocks.note: letters running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A famous person takes part in deceitful rows.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer or public figure, so the word is a direct synonym for a celebrity.

clue.text: Cooped up with wicked door-minder

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted or bent out of true, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter by letter as written

explanation.surface: Someone is trapped indoors with a nasty doorkeeper standing guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined to a single chamber, unable to leave it, is the plight of anyone kept shut in.

clue.text: Easily remembered feline found with small child at day's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: a cat is a feline
CH is a short form of child
last letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A cat and a toddler are discovered together at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune or slogan sticks in the memory readily, being appealing and simple to recall.

clue.text: Good discovered in self-controlled body

indicators.note: something discovered in another thing is found inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: continent means exercising self-restraint
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Virtue is found within a disciplined organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Continent here is the adjective meaning restrained, not a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of people forming part of a larger gathering, such as a delegation or troop.

clue.text: Encourage fights to get food containers

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
a boxer fights in the ring

explanation.surface: Someone eggs on brawlers in order to win some lunchboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartons made to hold eggs are packaging for a foodstuff, so they are receptacles for edible goods.

clue.text: No brother of mine, says 'Arry

blocks.note: surface reading: someone disowning a sibling
setter's reading: a Cockney, with dropped H, giving his rhyming-slang word for a female sibling

explanation.surface: A Londoner named Harry angrily disowns his brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, the London East End habit of replacing a word with a rhyming phrase, gives skin and blister for sister; 'Arry signals a Cockney speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not a brother but is a sibling is a sister, and this phrase is Cockney rhyming slang for her.

clue.text: The pest is in touch

indicators.note: in places the short word inside the synonym that follows

blocks.note: a touch can mean a subtle trace or shade
taken as written

explanation.surface: An annoying person is in contact with us.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an irritating person or thing, and a nuisance is exactly something that causes annoyance.

clue.text: See 15
It's tough no longer working in the theatre

blocks.note: ex means former, no longer so
performing on stage is acting

explanation.surface: Life is hard now that someone has retired from stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding great effort or precision, so a hard, demanding task can be called tough.

clue.text: See 4
To act as a drudge is hot and very difficult

blocks.note: to devil is to do routine work for a barrister or writer, as a junior hack
taken as written
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Doing menial chores is sweltering and hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a devil is a junior who does drudge work for a barrister or author, so to devil is to toil for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish informally means extremely hard or tricky, as in a devilish puzzle that is fiendishly tough.

clue.text: Fairness of eyes only half-visible when about to depart

indicators.note: if only half of a word can be seen, just its opening half is kept
about means surrounding, so the kept letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: the first half of the word eyes
to quit a place is to leave it

explanation.surface: Justice is blindfolded, her eyes half-covered as she prepares to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept half of 'eyes' wraps around the verb for leaving, giving E-QUIT-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is impartial justice and even-handedness, the principle of treating everyone fairly.

clue.text: A cry for help reveals Doris behind the hawthorn blossom

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the surname named first is placed second, following the blossom

blocks.note: may is a name for hawthorn blossom
Doris Day was a famous American singer and actress

explanation.surface: Someone calls out for assistance and Doris is discovered hiding behind a hawthorn bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayday is the international radio distress call used by ships and aircraft in grave danger.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil for an attractive girl, but no saint

definitions.text: for an attractive girl, but no saint

blocks.note: first meaning: a tool for crushing cooked potatoes

blocks.clueFragment: for an attractive girl, but no saint
blocks.note: second meaning: an old word for a dandy who pesters women he fancies

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' reads as a link, but it belongs to the second definition: a man who is keen on, or out for, a pretty girl, and not well behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato crusher is a common cooking tool, and a lady-killer who makes unwanted advances was dated slang of the same spelling.

clue.text: Protective specs for young women who have squealed first

blocks.note: to sing or squeal is slang for informing on someone
lasses are girls or young women

explanation.surface: Eyewear for girls who have been shrieking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the informer's verb ahead of the girls; sing and squeal are both underworld slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunglasses are tinted glasses worn to shield the eyes from bright light and glare.

clue.text: Dark fruit for a boyfriend?

blocks.note: first meaning: the brown sticky fruit of a palm
second meaning: a person one goes out with romantically

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as fruit offered to a boyfriend, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm bears brown, sweet fruit, and a romantic partner on an outing is also called this.

clue.text: Queen of Carthage achieved nothing

blocks.note: achieved means did, past tense
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A legendary ruler of an ancient city accomplished nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founder and ruler of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Being cultural helps to make Elizabeth nicer

indicators.note: letters that help to make up a phrase are part of it, so the word lies inside what follows

blocks.note: letters running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Exposure to the arts improves a woman called Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic relates to a group sharing traditions, customs and heritage, so it describes something cultural.

clue.text: The Bard's bawdy mistress is dried up

blocks.note: first meaning: the brothel keeper in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure
second meaning: cooked for too long until parched

explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare; Mistress Overdone runs a brothel in Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked too long becomes parched and leathery, and Shakespeare's bawd bears that very name.
